text.p: National Australia Bank Ltd said on Thursday that it was confident its performance would continue to improve in the current financial year.

The bank earlier reported a 6.8 percent rise in 1995/96 net profit to A$2.10 billion. NAB managing director Don Argus said he was confident the group's performance would improve despite strong competition in all markets and subdued economic activity.

"We are focussed on the fundamentals of our business; meeting customer needs, managing risks effectively and containing costs. We also have a vast potential market through our international spread of business units," Argus said in a statement accompanying the 1995/96 (October/September) results.
NAB said the surprisingly strong growth in the Australian economy last financial year was expected to moderate, with estimated growth of 2.5 percent in 1996/97 against four percent last year.
